definitions.explanation: Being at an early stage of life.
Having characteristics of a young child.

examples.japanese: {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}の{思|おも}い{出|で}。
{彼|かれ}は{幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}から{絵|え}が{好|す}きだった。
examples.english: He has liked drawing since he was very young.

examples.japanese: もう{大人|おとな}なのに、やることが{幼|おさな}くて{困|こま}る。
examples.english: Even though they're an adult, their behavior is so childish it's troubling.

notes:
{幼|おさな}い is an i-adjective describing early childhood (roughly ages 1-6) or childlike/immature qualities.

TWO MEANINGS:
1. Very young (neutral): {幼|おさな}い{子供|こども} (young child)
2. Immature/childish (negative): {考|かんが}えが{幼|おさな}い (thinking is immature)

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {幼|おさな}く
- Noun form: {幼|おさな}さ (youth, immaturity)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}: in early childhood
- {幼馴染|おさななじ}み: childhood friend
- {幼|おさな}い{顔|かお}: childlike face

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幼|おさな}い: very young (early childhood, or immature)
- {若|わか}い: young (broader age range, teens to young adults)
- {子供|こども}っぽい: childish (often pejorative)

RELATED:
- {幼児|ようじ}: infant, young child
- {幼稚園|ようちえん}: kindergarten
